description: An urban Internet of Things activity dataset with a synthetic DDoS attack generator, released with a five-page dataset paper at ACM SenSys 2021 by researchers at the University of Southern California. The raw data are the activity status of 4,060 event-driven IoT nodes deployed in an urban area, each with a node identifier, latitude, longitude and a timestamp recorded whenever its status changes, over one month. A script turns this into a benign dataset with a status for every node every 30 seconds, and a second script injects attacks with tunable numbers of nodes, duration, attack ratio and start time. A small feed-forward neural network shows how to label which nodes are under attack and when. Coverage: one anonymous city deployment; the paper does not name the city. Format and access: a free GitHub repository with the zipped dataset, scripts and model code; the repository LICENSE.md allows free use, modification and redistribution with citation but not for commercial purposes. Caveats: the attacks are synthetic and only binary activity is recorded, not packet traffic. Useful for testing cyber attack detection and resilience of sensor networks in public space and smart city infrastructure; related records are not yet linked.
